subject: project:gdl
value: ADDRESSED TO THE INTEGRATOR: six places where the run-29 residual schema contract fought the data, with what this lane did about each. (1) UPDATE PATH WAS UNDECIDABLE, so the contract's own word decided it. propose-record REFUSES any id that already exists in records/ or inbox/, so an accepted record can never be re-proposed; supersession would therefore have needed 971 NEW ids, and since 156 of 424 anchor functions already hold 3+ accepted attempts, doubling every record would have pushed 156 functions past the 5-per-function cap and made prune-attempts EJECT live records to make room for a mechanical field backfill. Supersession is also semantically wrong here: `supersedes` means the truth changed, and adding a derived index field changes no truth. This lane therefore did IN-PLACE field addition on its own branch (the contract says records 'GAIN optional object residual', which is additive language), gated by an integrity check asserting that the ONLY JSON-level change to any record is the added top-level `residual` key -- 971/971 passed, zero values mutated, zero keys removed. If the integrator wanted supersession, revert the 10 commits; nothing else in the tree depends on them. (2) NAME COLLISION: `attributes.residual` ALREADY EXISTS on 642 records and is a documented template field meaning 'what remains and why it was left' (free prose). The new object was therefore written at TOP LEVEL as `residual`, which does not collide -- but any tooling must not confuse `residual` (object) with `attributes.residual` (prose). (3) THE CONTRACT DUPLICATES AN EXISTING FIELD IT DOES NOT MENTION: a top-level `residual_class` already exists on 941/971 records and is SQL-indexed and queryable via `find --residual`. Its values have drifted to 38 distinct spellings (STRUCTURAL 280, 'REGISTER_ONLY/SCHEDULE (allocator or scheduler residual)' 187, NONE 154, ... down to 20 one-off free-text sentences). Normalising residual_class is probably worth more than any new field, and `family` should be defined against it explicitly rather than beside it. (4) THE STARTER VOCABULARY CONTAINS FAMILIES THE CORPUS DOES NOT EXHIBIT AS RESIDUALS: pool-order and reloc-naming appear almost exclusively as causes FOUND AND FIXED, not as what remains (1 genuine pool-order residual corpus-wide). Conversely the vocabulary has no term for the single largest class: 155 records whose residual is NONE. This lane used 'no-residual' and flags it as a needed vocabulary addition. (5) THE CONTRACT ASSUMES SIGNATURE IS IN THE PROSE; MOSTLY IT IS NOT. Only 297/971 records mention any opcode token at all. Live measurement is the better source and is cheap: an fndiff --ops sweep over the 71 TUs owning attempt records took ~6 minutes and produced machine-measured signatures for 624/971. 347 have none because the function is webfrank/p6frank-referenced (108 of 424 attempt functions -- fndiff scores the POSTPROCESSED object, so those read exact by construction per AGENTS.md discipline 10) or measures matched; each such record says which, in words, rather than carrying a silent null. (6) FIELDS ADDED BEYOND THE CONTRACT, flagged for approval: `confidence`, `signature_source`, `extraction_status`, and `family_candidate` + `family_candidate_confidence`. These exist because family extraction measured 30-50% precise (see claim.BF_residual-family-cannot-be-back-extracted-from-attempt-prose.20260901.v1): rather than write guesses into `family` and poison every future query, unverified guesses are QUARANTINED in `family_candidate` (124 records) while `family` itself carries only hand-verified (26) or structured-field-derived (150) values, and 795 records carry an explicit 'measured-dead, not never-attempted' extraction_status. If the integrator prefers the bare 4-key contract, drop the extra keys -- but then either drop the 124 candidates entirely or accept known-unreliable families in the queryable field.
